title: Medical / biomedical company
description: An operating company in medicine or the life sciences — the thing investors put money INTO. Strictly disjoint from entity.schema.json, which describes the investors. A firm that both operates and invests (e.g. a pharma with a CVC arm) is recorded twice: the operating business here, the venture arm there, linked by name. Companies are in scope regardless of whether they ever raised venture capital; the funding block is optional so bootstrapped and state-owned players still fit.

id.description: Stable slug, region-prefixed to match the investor convention: 'us-abridge', 'eu-oviva', 'jp-preferred-networks'.

local.description: Name in local language/script if applicable

aka.description: Former names, tickers, common abbreviations. Feeds the link resolver — a company renamed after a merger is still reachable from an investor's older portfolio listing.

category.description: Primary bucket. Deliberately drawn from the SAME vocabulary as an investor's strategy.sector_focus (taxonomy.json > sectors) so a sector filter crosses cleanly between the two directories.

sectors.description: Secondary buckets, same vocabulary. Most companies straddle two or three.

status.description: Corporate status, NOT clinical status. 'public' covers any listed venue; the exchange goes in exit.ticker.

profile.description: What the company actually does and how far along it is.

what.description: One sentence, concrete and checkable. 'Ambient AI scribe that drafts clinical notes from the patient visit' — not 'transforming healthcare with AI'.

modalities.description: taxonomy.json > modalities. Shared with investors, so a fund's stated modality focus lines up with real companies.

development_stage.description: For therapeutics use the trial phase of the LEAD asset; for devices/software use pilot -> commercial. 'approved' means a regulator cleared it; 'commercial' means it is selling.

lead_asset.description: Therapeutics only: the lead program name/target, e.g. 'BNT327 (PD-L1xVEGF bispecific)'.

regulatory.description: Clearances and designations actually granted. Do not list applications or intentions.

body.description: FDA / EMA / CE / PMDA / NMPA / MFDS / TFDA / MHRA / TGA / CDSCO

kind.description: 510(k) / De Novo / PMA / CE-MDR / NDA / BLA / Breakthrough Device / orphan-drug / fast-track

item.description: Product or program the clearance covers

funding.description: Optional — absent means unknown or never raised, which are different things; say which in verification_notes when it matters.

unicorn.description: true only with a sourced >=$1B valuation

rounds.description: Newest first. Partial history is fine and expected.

investors.description: THE LINK. Written by researchers as plain names; scripts/build_companies.py resolves each to an investor id where one exists in this directory and leaves entity_id null otherwise. Never hand-write entity_id — a stale hand-written id outlives the rename that broke it.

name.description: As reported, e.g. 'General Catalyst', 'a16z Bio + Health'

entity_id.description: DERIVED by the build. Points at an id in all-entities.json, or null when that investor is not (yet) in this directory.

round.description: Which round they came in at, e.g. 'series-b'

sources.description: Provenance. Every quantitative claim should be traceable to a quote here.

confidence.description: high = official/primary; medium = reputable secondary; low = single weak/old source or inference

researched_by.description: agent segment id that produced this row

money.description: Money kept as reported (raw) to avoid fabricated conversions; usd optional when confidently derivable.

raw.description: As reported, e.g. '$30M', '€12.5M', '¥50億'; null if unknown
